primitives.name: Input Sensitivity Test
primitives.verbatim_quote: # GATE PERTURBATION BATTERY (Motif, 2026-11-07) Purpose: the consumption test the wiring night is built around — does the Python catalog gate's output actually move when game inputs move?
primitives.assumptions: Gate output varies monotonically with input perturbations; environment controls are independent variables.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input changes exceed threshold, gate output shifts beyond noise floor.

layer2.mapping: Maps environmental deltas to probabilistic gate responses via binary classification of input regimes.
layer2.telemetry: Change in normalized gate output relative to baseline.

primitives.name: Regime Activation Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Verdict: the gate is input-sensitive and family-activation is regime-driven (wind alone activates all 279 families).
primitives.assumptions: Wind speed acts as a universal trigger for family activation; other factors act additively.
primitives.breakdown_regime: All 279 families activate at wind speed ≥ 8 mph.

layer2.mapping: Derives activation probability from scalar wind condition using empirical frequency data.
layer2.telemetry: Number of activated families under given environmental constraint.

primitives.name: Contextual Dialect Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The integration risk is not the gate — it is the caller dialect: context keys must match the extractor's expected names, and nothing in the tree validates that mapping.
primitives.assumptions: Mismatched keys produce silent identity mappings; validation is external to gate logic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when caller provides non-matching key bindings.

layer2.mapping: Ensures semantic alignment between caller and extractor contexts via key-set intersection.
layer2.telemetry: Boolean flag indicating successful key binding resolution.
